title: A systematic scanning method to locate cryptic terrestrial species
author: Findlay-Robinson, Hill

steps.title: Assemble scanning array and GPS
steps.instruction: Gather the HPR Plus reader, BP Plus portable antenna, and combine them as the “scanning array”. Also prepare a Garmin Etrex 10 GPS unit and biodegradable flagging tape for field marking.

steps.title: Prepare PIT‑tagged simulated dormouse
steps.instruction: Insert a Peddymark Mini ISO microchip (dimensions 1.4 × 8 mm) into a piece of cooled cooked sausage, then embed the sausage inside woven grass to mimic a hibernating dormouse (the “simulated dormouse”).

steps.title: Measure detection distance on four substrates
steps.instruction: Place the simulated dormouse at a known location on each of four substrates (bare ground, a thin layer of soil, under rocks, under a log). Using the scanning array, sweep the area and record the maximum distance at which the tag is detected for each substrate. Record the observed detection distances (range 7–22 cm, mean 12.92 ± 5.07 cm). Note that substrate did not significantly affect read distance (ANOVA F = 0.17, df = 3, p = 0.91).

substeps.instruction: Set up substrate and place simulated dormouse.
Sweep with scanning array while moving side‑to‑side.
Measure and log the farthest detection distance.

steps.title: Delimit 5000 m² search area with flagging tape
steps.instruction: In the field, mark a rectangular area of approximately 71 m × 71 m (≈ 5000 m²) using biodegradable flagging tape.

steps.title: Subdivide area into ~71 m × 10–15 m sections
steps.instruction: Divide the marked area into smaller strips roughly 71 m long and 10–15 m wide (width adjusted to habitat type) to create manageable transect blocks.

steps.title: Place simulated dormouse cryptically and record GPS
steps.instruction: A field assistant hides the simulated dormouse in a cryptic position within one of the subdivided sections while the operator is absent, then records the exact GPS coordinates of the placement using the Garmin unit.

steps.title: Conduct systematic transect sweeps with scanning array
steps.instruction: For each subdivided section, walk parallel transects along the width of the block, sweeping the ground continuously with the scanning array. Space successive transect lines 1–1.5 m apart to ensure a small overlap of scanned area. Maintain a side‑to‑side sweeping motion of the antenna throughout. Perform this procedure for a total of 15 blind trials (five trials in each of the three habitat classifications: mature, mid‑aged, and young woodland).

substeps.instruction: Start at one edge of the section.
Walk a straight line while holding the scanning array low to the ground and moving it side‑to‑side.
Shift 1–1.5 m laterally and repeat until the entire section is covered.
Repeat the whole process for all sections and for all 15 trials.

steps.title: Record detection outcome, distance, and time
steps.instruction: During each blind trial, note whether the simulated dormouse is located. If found, record the time elapsed from the start of scanning to detection (mean successful time 168 ± 73 min; overall detection success 73%). Also record the detection distance (as measured in step 3). Report that habitat type did not affect detection likelihood (Binomial GLM p = 0.84) nor time to locate (ANOVA F = 0.10, df = 2, p = 0.90). For successful trials, the number of replicates per habitat were: mature N = 3, mid‑aged n = 4, young n = 4.
